A sub-app's own [`ErrorHandler`](#errorhandler), `Views` and `ViewsLayout` still apply to the requests under its mount path, but only when the whole mount path, from the top-level app down, is literal. Under a parameter, as in `app.Use("/t/:tenant", tenantApp)`, the routes match and run while the nearest enclosing mount with a literal path, or the top-level app, supplies the error handler and the view engine. A [`Domain`](#domain) mount matches a parameterized path as a pattern, so its sub-app keeps its own. The [`RegexHandler`](./fiber.md#regexhandler) of a sub-app mounted on the top-level app compiles the `regex()` constraints in the full path of every route below it, the mount prefix included, so an app mounted deeper does not use its own.
:::

| <Reference id="readbuffersize">ReadBufferSize</Reference>                             | `int`                                                           | per-connection buffer size for requests' reading. This also limits the maximum header size: a request whose headers do not fit is answered `431 Request Header Fields Too Large`. Increase this buffer if your clients send multi-KB RequestURIs and/or multi-KB headers \(for example, BIG cookies\). Zero or negative values fall back to the default, `fiber.DefaultReadBufferSize`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `8192`                                                                 |
| <Reference id="readtimeout">ReadTimeout</Reference>                                   | `time.Duration`                                                 | The amount of time allowed to read the full request, including the body. The default timeout is unlimited.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `0`                                                                    |
| <Reference id="reducememoryusage">ReduceMemoryUsage</Reference>                       | `bool`                                                          | Aggressively reduces memory usage at the cost of higher CPU usage if set to true.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `false`                                                                |
| <Reference id="regexhandler">RegexHandler</Reference>                                 | `any`                                                           | Configures the compiler used for `regex()` route constraints. Assign `regexp.MustCompile` or `coregex.MustCompile` directly to switch engines. It must be a function of the form `func(string) T`, where `T` has a `MatchString(string) bool` method; `fiber.New` panics for anything else. Fiber reuses the compiled matcher across requests, so the returned value must be safe for concurrent use. Fiber may invoke `RegexHandler` more than once per route while parsing raw and normalized route patterns during registration.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `regexp.MustCompile`                                                   |

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
